# Surplus Secure

> Surplus Secure helps Michigan homeowners recover surplus funds left over after a
> property tax foreclosure sale. It is run by Kelli Meeks, a licensed Michigan
> attorney with 40 years of real estate law experience, and works on contingency —
> there is no upfront cost to the client.

## Core Resources

- [Homepage](https://surplussecure.com/): What surplus funds are, who can claim them, how the recovery process works, and how to start a free consultation.

## What surplus funds are

When a Michigan county forecloses on a property for unpaid taxes and sells it at
auction for more than the owner owed, the difference is called surplus. Under
Michigan law that surplus belongs to the former property owner, not the county.
Example: a home sells for $100,000 against $25,000 owed in taxes, penalties, fees
and the 5% county commission — the remaining $75,000 is surplus owed to the owner.

## Who can claim

The legal owner of the property at the time of foreclosure has the right to claim
the surplus proceeds. If that owner has died, their heirs may be eligible to file.

## Deadlines

Michigan law sets strict filing deadlines for surplus claims. Missing them means
the county or the state keeps the money permanently. Michigan law also allows the
county or state to hold surplus funds for up to 10 months following the auction.

## Cost

No upfront cost. Surplus Secure works on a contingency fee — a percentage of the
surplus actually recovered. No recovery, no fee.

## About

Surplus Secure is a Michigan legal service focused solely on tax-foreclosure
surplus fund recovery. Lead attorney Kelli Meeks has practiced real estate law for
40 years. The practice handles the full claim: reviewing the foreclosure record,
calculating the surplus owed, preparing and filing the claim, and tracking every
statutory deadline through to the release of funds.
